workflow.openDatabaseTitle:
Resume an existing Rumcet DB.
The DAT, scanned folders and matching results are kept: no need to start over.
workflow.loadDatTitle:
Step 1: create a new Rumcet DB from a DAT/XML file (local or downloaded).
A DAT/XML is the complete inventory of a system's games and of the files that make them up, made by preservation groups (No-Intro, Redump, MAME…).
If a Rumcet DB is already open, adds a complementary DAT (e.g. CHDs DAT, BIOS pack).
workflow.addFolderTitle:
Step 2: add a folder containing your ROMs.
RUMCET analyzes the files and the content of archives (ZIP, 7z, RAR, CHD…) and computes their checksums.
workflow.matchTitle:
Step 3: compare your files' checksums with those of the DAT/XML.
You then see complete, incomplete or missing games, and extra files.
workflow.selectTitle:
Step 4 (optional): choose the games to consolidate. By default, all games are selected.
You can check or uncheck them by hand while browsing the DAT/XML content (left pane, “DAT/XML file” section), or use the automatic selection, which is recommended (regions, languages, clones, prototypes…, 1G1R).
workflow.consolidateTitle:
Step 5: rebuild the selected games in the target folder, renamed according to the DAT/XML and in the format defined by the consolidation profile.
Depending on your settings, it can also clean up your source folders: delete game files already rebuilt and move unneeded files to dedicated folders.

welcome.title: Welcome to RUMCET
welcome.tagline: RUMCET checks your ROM collection against a reference DAT/XML, then renames, cleans up and converts it to the formats of your choice.
welcome.automation: RUMCET can automate much of the work: downloading DAT/XML files and missing games from within the app, picking the best compression format for each game, creating .m3u files for multi-disc games, moving unneeded files rather than deleting them… You choose what is automated, and how.
welcome.step1: Create a Rumcet DB from a DAT/XML file (local or downloaded) or open an existing Rumcet DB
welcome.step3: Match the ROMs to identify missing ROMs or files
welcome.step4: Optional: choose the games to consolidate, by hand while browsing the DAT/XML content (left pane) or with the automatic selection (recommended)

help.step1:
A DAT/XML file is the complete inventory of an emulated system's games and of the files that make up each of them (names, sizes, checksums), made by retro game preservation groups such as No-Intro (cartridges), Redump (discs) or MAME (arcade).

RUMCET can download it for you, then creates a Rumcet DB from it: the database that will hold the DAT, your scanned folders and the matching results.

To resume your work, use “Open Rumcet DB”.
help.step2:
Add one or more folders containing your ROMs. RUMCET records the names, sizes and checksums of every file, including inside archives, without you having to extract them.

A new scan only re-analyzes what has changed.
help.step3:
Matching compares your files' checksums (CRC32, then MD5/SHA1) with those of the DAT/XML, whatever the file names.

You then see complete, incomplete or missing games, as well as extra files.
help.step4:
By default, all games of the DAT/XML are selected for consolidation. This step is optional, but it lets you keep only the games you care about.

By hand: click the DAT/XML in the left pane (“DAT/XML file” section) to browse its content (search, filters, grouping), then check or uncheck games.

Automatically (recommended): the automatic selection applies rules (regions, languages, clones, prototypes, BIOS…) and 1G1R (one game, one ROM). The settings are saved in the Rumcet DB and can serve as a template for a system.
help.step5:
Consolidation rebuilds the selected games in the target folder: each file is renamed according to the DAT/XML, in the format chosen by the consolidation profile (ZIP, 7z, CHD, per-system compatibility…).

Depending on your cleanup settings, it can also clean up your source folders: delete the game files already rebuilt in the target folder, and move unneeded or unreferenced files to dedicated folders rather than deleting them.

archives.m3uPriorityNotice: 💿 .m3u creation is enabled for this profile: multi-disc games ignore 7Z and ZIP. Their discs are produced as CHD (if allowed for the system), otherwise as raw files. See the "Multi-disc" tab.
archives.compressionLevelInfo: Determines the compression level for ZIP/7Z archives
archives.recreate: Recreate archives that are already perfect
archives.recreateInfo: If disabled, archives whose format and content already match will be copied directly without recompression
archives.bestCompression: Try all compatible formats and keep the smallest
archives.bestCompressionWarning:
⚠️ WARNING: This option slows down the process CONSIDERABLY!

The application will create an archive in EVERY compatible format for each game and keep only the one with the smallest size.

  • Processing time: 3x to 5x slower
  • CPU usage: Maximum
  • Disk usage: Temporarily doubled

Recommended only if final disk space is critical.
archives.bestCompressionInfo: For each game, all compatible archive variants are created, then only the most compact one is kept (very slow)
archives.solidInfo: Solid compression improves the compression ratio but slows down extraction
archives.multithreadingInfo: Uses multiple processor cores to speed up compression

cleanup.enableInfo: If disabled, source folders remain untouched and ROMs are simply copied
cleanup.scopeInfo:
Cleanup runs right after each game is consolidated.
"Used files only": only the copies used to consolidate the game are deleted; unused duplicates stay.
"All matched files": every copy of the consolidated game's files is deleted.
Inside a ZIP/7z archive, only the files that are no longer needed are removed; the archive is deleted only when nothing in it is needed anymore. Produced files and files of other games in the target folder are never deleted.
cleanup.protectUnselected: Keep files used by unselected games
cleanup.protectUnselectedInfo: If enabled, a file will not be deleted if it matches a DAT game that is not checked for consolidation
cleanup.moveUnmatched: Move unmatched files to the dedicated folder
cleanup.moveUnmatchedInfo: Files that do not match any DAT game are moved to the folder below, grouped by source folder. Those inside a ZIP/7z archive that is still needed are split out into a separate archive. Files in the target folder are never moved.
cleanup.readOnlyArchives: Non-modifiable archives (RAR, CHD, CSO) containing unmatched files:
cleanup.readOnlyArchivesInfo: Applies when none of the DAT files in the archive is needed anymore. If some still are, the archive stays in place.
cleanup.unmatchedFolderGlobal: The destination folder is a global setting, shared by all profiles: "Folders" tab.
cleanup.unmatchedMultiSystemOn: Multi-system target folders enabled: files will go into one subfolder per system (e.g. {example})

multiDisc.generateM3u: Create a .m3u file for multi-disc / multi-media games
multiDisc.generateM3uInfo: Games split into several DAT entries — "(Disc 1)", "(Disk 1 of 2)", "(Tape 1)", "(Side A)"… — get a <game>.m3u file placed next to their discs, which lets the emulator swap discs. Only systems that accept .m3u files are affected; arcade DATs are ignored. Only selected and consolidated discs are listed.
multiDisc.warning: ⚠️ Impact on compression: a .m3u cannot reference a 7Z or ZIP archive. When this option is enabled, the discs of multi-disc games are never compressed to 7Z or ZIP, whatever the format priority order: they are produced as CHD if that format is allowed for the system (and the disc has a .cue / .gdi / .iso entry point), otherwise copied as raw files. Single-disc games keep the usual compression.

arcade.setModeInfo: Specific to MAME DATs (with parent / clone / BIOS relationships). Determines how RUMCET will organize your ROMs on disk after consolidation. This setting is ignored for non-arcade DATs (No-Intro / Redump). See docs/arcade-set-modes.md for details on the modes and their differences.
arcade.split: Split — each clone contains only its own ROMs
arcade.splitInfo: The parent and BIOS remain separate archives. Compact, but each clone depends on the parent + BIOS to work. Recommended mode.
arcade.nonMergedInfo: The clone's archive contains its own ROMs AND the ROMs shared with its parent. Large (duplication), but each game works without depending on the parent (the BIOS remains separate).
arcade.merged: Merged — one archive per family (parent + all its clones)
arcade.mergedInfo: The parent's archive contains the ROMs of the parent and all its clones. Very compact, but incompatible with some emulators that expect a separate archive per game.
arcade.layoutInfo: How files are laid out in the target folder after consolidation. Specific to MAME DATs.
arcade.separateBiosInfo: BIOS sets (isbios) are stored in bios/ instead of flat alongside games.
arcade.separateBiosWarning:
⚠️ Incompatible with standard MAME

Original MAME expects BIOS archives in the same folder as the ROMs. If you move them into bios/, games that depend on them will not launch, unless your frontend supports a separate BIOS path (Recalbox convention).
arcade.chdEmptyZip: Create an empty .zip for CHD-only games
arcade.chdEmptyZipInfo: For a game with no regular ROMs (CHD only), creates an empty <game>.zip placeholder next to the <game>/ subfolder. Recalbox lists games via the .zip files present. Implies storing the CHD in a subfolder.

oneGameOneRom.title: 1G1R — 1 game, 1 ROM
oneGameOneRom.tabIntro: These values are the starting point for a system that has no saved model yet. The settings actually applied to a database are edited in Auto select, from the main window, and belong to that database alone.
oneGameOneRom.enableInfo: Decides whether 1G1R starts out ticked for a new database. Automatic selection then keeps a single version per game, arbitrating variants according to the priorities below. Nothing is applied until you click “Apply” in the automatic selection screen.
oneGameOneRom.priorityInfo: The first entry of each list wins. A value missing from a list is not excluded: it simply comes last. To firmly exclude a region or a language, use an automatic selection rule.
oneGameOneRom.regionPriority: Regions, from most to least preferred:
oneGameOneRom.languagePriority: Languages, from most to least preferred:
oneGameOneRom.videoPriority: Video modes, from most to least preferred:
oneGameOneRom.languageOverRegionInfo: To prefer "the French version wherever it comes from" rather than "the Europe version".
oneGameOneRom.preferLatestRevisionInfo: At equal regional quality, (Rev 2) beats (Rev 1), which beats the original untagged edition.
oneGameOneRom.fallbackToOwned: Fall back to a version I own
oneGameOneRom.fallbackToOwnedInfo: When the preferred version is missing from your collection but another one is present, keep the one you own instead of leaving a hole. Uncheck to apply the priorities to the letter: the game will then be reported as missing until the preferred version turns up.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListInfo: The same game is sometimes released under unrelated names depending on the region — Pokémon Version Or, Pokémon Goldene Edition and Pocket Monsters Kin are all Pokémon Gold. Clone lists record these relations, which no title analysis can guess, so that 1G1R keeps a single one of them.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListSourceInfo: URL of the folder containing the .json files. Change it to use a mirror or a fork.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListFolderInfo: Where downloaded clone lists are stored. Leave empty to use the application data folder.
oneGameOneRom.cloneListAutoUpdate: Keep clone lists up to date automatically
oneGameOneRom.cloneListAutoUpdateInfo: On each DAT load and each time a database is opened, RUMCET checks whether the clone list for that system has been updated, downloads it if so, then applies it. When unchecked, RUMCET uses the clone lists already present in the local folder and downloads nothing. Either way, you can update the clone list at any time by right-clicking the DAT/XML file in the left panel.

descriptions.universal: For maximum compatibility: only formats read by every emulator (core) of a system are kept.
descriptions.recalbox: To play on Recalbox: formats accepted by at least one emulator of the system are kept, and .m3u files are created for multi-disc games.
descriptions.master: To archive a collection: 7z, ZIP and CHD (when the system allows it), keeping the most compact format for each game.
descriptions.custom: Your personal profile, to set up as you like.
descriptions.user: Custom profile, to set up as you like.

profiles.help:
A consolidation profile groups the compression, per-system compatibility, cleanup, arcade and 1G1R settings. The current profile is chosen in the main window.

100% compatibility: formats read by every emulator of a system.

Recalbox (play): formats accepted by at least one Recalbox emulator, .m3u files for multi-disc games.

Archive / Master: 7z, ZIP or CHD, the most compact format for each game.

Built-in profiles can be edited and reset; the + button creates your own profile from the displayed one.

help.step1:
A DAT/XML file is the complete inventory of an emulated system's games and of the files that make up each of them (names, sizes, checksums), made by retro game preservation groups (No-Intro, Redump, MAME…). It is the reference your ROMs will be compared against.

Pick a file from your disk or download it here.

If no Rumcet DB is open, the DAT creates a new Rumcet DB. Otherwise, it is merged as a complementary DAT (e.g. CHDs DAT, BIOS pack).
help.sources:
No-Intro covers cartridge and floppy games, Redump disc-based games (CD, DVD…). Pick the source offered for the system.

No-Intro DATs cannot be downloaded automatically: “Open page” opens the website in your browser, then select the downloaded file via “Local file”.
help.mameSources:
For arcade, pick the MAME version used by your emulator: ROMs change from one version to another.

Progetto-Snaps provides the full DAT (parent/clone relationships, BIOS, emulation status), required by the advanced arcade features. Pleasuredome offers DATs already organized by mode (split, merged, non-merged, CHDs).
help.step2:
The Rumcet DB is a database (.sqlite file) dedicated to this DAT: it holds the DAT inventory, your scanned folders and the matching results.

It is created automatically in your Rumcet DB folder (set in the settings); you can reopen it later with “Open Rumcet DB”.
help.step3:
The target folder receives the games rebuilt by the consolidation. If it already contains ROMs, they are scanned and taken into account.

Working folders (unreferenced, incomplete, temporary ROMs) are optional: left empty, they use those from the settings. All of them can be changed later.

dbFolders.targetInfo: The ROMs kept by the consolidation are placed in this folder. It is scanned right after the Rumcet DB is created, which may take a while if it already contains files.
dbFolders.systemSubfolder: Create a subfolder named after the system
dbFolders.systemSubfolderInfo: Example: …/psx. The system is detected from the DAT name (or chosen manually).
dbFolders.advancedInfo: Specific to this Rumcet DB. Leave a field empty to use the folder defined in the settings.
